target_state: implemented staging handoff. The whole 64-instruction body, its five direct callees, its three indirect dispatches and its complete stack frame were re-derived from the image bytes for this package. The frame arithmetic is the load-bearing part: it is the only thing that pins the two dispatch cleanups, and it is what makes every stack-relative displacement in the listing land on a field of the one frame object. Three callee bodies were read in full to fix the record layout (0x0041ea00, 0x00427fd0, 0x0093db80) and two more for their terminators and one SEH frame (0x006b1f90, 0x006b4b60).

intended_paths.status: staging-only handoff; no canonical path is claimed and no other package's files were touched

implementation.linkage: C language linkage, declared in the package header so the validator can resolve the span from the symbol name
implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX only, aliased into ESI at 0x00f9b7f4 and never moved back; no ordinary stack arguments. The terminator is a bare RET (byte C3 at 0x00f9b8b0), so the callee pops nothing.
implementation.return_type: void (INFERRED from the listing; see return_semantics and unresolved_questions)
implementation.receiver_model: an opaque 0x818-byte run with only the three displacements this body reaches named: +0x00 (the word 0x00f9b83a loads and follows to a table), +0x28 (the gate object, read three times) and +0x814 (compared against the candidate, and the address handed to 0x00427fd0). The body writes NO byte of the receiver on any path, and the model test asserts that at the byte level. The machine-derived receiver record for this VA enumerates exactly those three displacements (receiver.offsets = [0, 40, 2068], register ECX, written_through 0), so no member is named.
implementation.dispatch_model: three indirect transfers, all typed function pointers declared in the package header and all installed as observers by the model test. Two are on the object the receiver holds at +0x28 (table entries at +0x24 and +0x14); one is on the receiver itself (table entry at +0x80). None has an address: each is read out of a table the object names through its leading word, so no callee listing exists to consult. Each is called with its receiver in ECX.
implementation.dependency_note: all five direct callees are declared extern in the package header and defined as observers in the package's own model test. No other package's files were read or written.

The header alone also compiles clean under the same flags via a one-line wrapper translation unit.

function_extent.listing_reexported: the 193 bytes at 0x00f9b7f0 were re-read from the image and every instruction boundary, branch target, call target and displacement was checked against them. The five direct CALL rel32 values were also recomputed by hand from their bytes and match the recorded targets: 0x00f9b824 -> 0x0041ea00, 0x00f9b862 -> 0x00427fd0, 0x00f9b898 -> 0x006b1f90, 0x00f9b8a2 -> 0x006b4b60, 0x00f9b887 -> 0x0093db80. 0x00f9b7f0 is preceded by sixteen CC bytes (0x00f9b7e0..0x00f9b7ef) and 0x00f9b8b0 is followed by fifteen (0x00f9b8b1..0x00f9b8bf), so the entry and the RET are the island's own boundaries and the body is 64 instructions with no hidden continuation.

observed_original_abi.callee_conventions: each fixed by the callee's own last bytes, read from the image. 0x0041ea00 ends 0x0041ea5d MOV ESP,EBP / 0x0041ea5f POP EBP / 0x0041ea60 RET (C3) -> __thiscall with no stack words, removes 0. 0x00427fd0 ends 0x00428051 C2 04 00 -> __thiscall, one stack word, removes 4. 0x0093db80 ends 0x0093dbb7 C2 04 00 -> __thiscall, one stack word read as a byte, removes 4. 0x006b1f90 ends 0x006b1fb2 POP ECX / 0x006b1fb3 RET (C3) -> cdecl, removes 0. 0x006b4b60 ends 0x006b4caa ADD ESP,0x18 / 0x006b4cad RET (C3) -> cdecl, removes 0, inside its own SEH frame.
observed_original_abi.dispatch_conventions: INFERRED, and this is the one inference the package rests on. The two dispatches have no address, so their terminators cannot be read. Both are pinned at 8 bytes of net cleanup by the frame (0x00f9b813: 0x28 - x + 4 = 0x24; 0x00f9b878: the block pushes 36 and retires 20, so its five callees must remove 16, and 4 + x + 4 + 0 + 0 = 16), and 8 is the ordinary value for a two-word callee that owns its cleanup. See unresolved_questions.

mechanics.body_shape: gate on the object the receiver holds at +0x28; ask that object's table entry at +0x24 for property 0x03ad556a into an 0x18-byte frame object; if the answer is non-zero and the halfword at +0x12 of the frame's published pointer is 0x0a, ask 0x0041ea00 for a pointer and load the dword behind it; if that equals the receiver's own word at +0x814 stop; otherwise call the receiver's table entry at +0x80, pre-load the record at frame+0x04 with type 0x0a and flags 0x0002, hand it to 0x00427fd0 together with the ADDRESS of the receiver's +0x814 word, ask the +0x28 object's table entry at +0x14 for the same property into the same record, and if the record's +0x10 byte has bit 0x04 call 0x0093db80 on that record with the argument 0; then look 0x031389b5 up with 0x006b1f90 and bind the result to the +0x28 object through 0x006b4b60.

frame_resolution.method: one linear walk of committed stack bytes through all 64 instructions. `committed` is entry_ESP minus the current ESP, so it grows with every SUB/PUSH and shrinks with every ADD/POP; a call's contribution is the negative of whatever its callee removes. Entry edge: committed is 0x1c at 0x00f9b7fb. Epilogue: 0x00f9b8aa pops three words and 0x00f9b8ad drops 0x18, so both the 0x00f9b838 edge and the fall-through from 0x00f9b8a7 must arrive at 0x24, and 0x00f9b8ac must then find 0x18 so that ADD ESP,0x18 lands on entry.
frame_resolution.slow_path_ledger: committed is 0x24 at 0x00f9b838. The block 0x00f9b83a..0x00f9b8a7 pushes 36 bytes (4 for 0x00427fd0's argument, 8 for the +0x14 dispatch, 4 for 0x0093db80's, 12 for 0x006b1f90's, 8 for 0x006b4b60's), the five callees remove 16, and the body retires 20 itself with ADD ESP,0x4 at 0x00f9b89d and ADD ESP,0x10 at 0x00f9b8a7 -- 36 - 16 - 20 = 0, so the block is net zero and 0x00f9b8aa arrives at exactly 0x24. The model test asserts each of those three numbers separately.
frame_resolution.corroboration: three independent agreements. (1) The frame requirement pins both dispatch cleanups at 8 with no freedom left, and no other assignment of the three callee-terminator cleanups closes both edges. (2) Only with 8 at 0x00f9b878 does every stack-relative address in the listing land on a field of the frame object: with 4, 0x00f9b87a would test entry-0x08, four bytes below the flags word 0x00f9b85d wrote, and 0x0093db80 would receive the frame object instead of the record 0x00427fd0 was handed. (3) The two pre-stores then land on exactly the two fields 0x00427fd0's own listing reads (+0x10 and +0x12 of its receiver), and the guard byte lands on the very flags word 0x00f9b85d wrote. A walk that produced that from a wrong boundary would be a coincidence four times over.
frame_resolution.not_closed_by: nothing in this package closes the frame by reading the dispatch targets' own terminators, because they have no address. That is the residual risk and it is recorded in unresolved_questions rather than papered over.

Its split is a leading dword at +0x00 and a 0x14-byte record at +0x04, and that split is the only one under which the two pre-stores and the guard byte land on the fields 0x00427fd0 is documented to read: 4 + 0x14 == 0x18 exactly, and every one of the five stack-relative addresses resolves onto a field of it.

mechanics.control_flow: six conditional branches, all with absolute targets inside the recovered body span 0x00f9b7f0..0x00f9b8b0, and no loop of any kind: JZ 0x00f9b8ac at 0x00f9b7fb (the null gate), JZ 0x00f9b82b at 0x00f9b817 (a false dispatch answer), JNZ 0x00f9b82b at 0x00f9b822 (a type word that is not 0x0a), JZ 0x00f9b8aa at 0x00f9b838 (the candidate already matches), JZ 0x00f9b88c at 0x00f9b87f (the guard bit is clear), plus the retarget 0x00f9b817/0x00f9b822 -> 0x00f9b82b. Three edges reach the epilogue: 0x00f9b7fb -> 0x00f9b8ac, 0x00f9b838 -> 0x00f9b8aa, and the fall-through from 0x00f9b8a7. The body is acyclic and executes at most eight transfers.
mechanics.arm_decision: the candidate starts at 0 (0x00f9b811 XOR EDI,EDI) and is replaced by exactly one load, 0x00f9b829 `MOV EDI,[EAX]`, and only when the dispatch answered non-zero AND the type word was 0x0a. So the 0x00f9b82b compare has a defined left side on every path, and a false dispatch answer is not an early exit: it makes the candidate 0, which then still has to differ from the receiver's +0x814 word for the body to continue. The model test's C1/C1b pair pins exactly that.
mechanics.exact_compare_not_lower_bound: 0x00f9b82b/0x00f9b838 is CMP/JZ, i.e. exact 32-bit equality, not a range or an ordering. The model test's G group drives 0x80000000 against 0x7fffffff and the mirror, which a signed `<` model would resolve differently, and 0xffffffff against itself, which only an equality model resolves as a match.
mechanics.not_modelled: the three saved registers and the two ADD ESP instructions as executed code; the +0x80 entry's EAX and 0x006b4b60's AL, neither of which any path reads; the identity of the three table entries; the two direct callees 0x00427fd0 and 0x0093db80 make internally (0x00427fd0's other arm would call 0x0093dd80, a callee of 0x00427fd0 that this body never reaches); and 0x006b4b60's SEH scope, which the body enters and leaves normally.
mechanics.globals: none. The complete 64-instruction listing names no data-segment address, and neither does the source span. 0x0152fdc4 and 0x0152fdc8 appear only inside 0x006b1f90, and 0x015d1164 only inside 0x0041ea00; both are recorded here as callee-internal and are deliberately not used as evidence for anything in this body.

mechanics.return_semantics_machine: void, INFERRED. Nothing is moved into EAX for a caller on any of the three edges: 0x00f9b8ac is reached with EAX still holding the table entry 0x00f9b803 loaded, 0x00f9b8aa is reached with 0x00427fd0's return in EAX, and the fall-through is reached with 0x006b4b60's return in EAX. The three edges leave three different dead words in EAX and none of them is the result of anything. The records do not settle it -- abi.return_semantics says 'unclassified_in_EAX' and ghidra_function.return_type says 'undefined' -- so this is stated as an inference and named in unresolved_questions.
mechanics.receiver_writes: none. The complete 64-instruction listing contains no store whose effective address is derived from ESI or ECX. The only stores in the body are the two halfword stores into its own frame at 0x00f9b84e and 0x00f9b85d; everything else that changes memory happens inside a callee, and the two that this body hands a pointer to are handed frame addresses, not receiver addresses. The model test asserts the whole 0x818 bytes are byte-identical before and after the full path.

return_semantics.value: no value is produced. The only outputs are the effect on the frame object (which dies with the call) and the three calls the body makes into the object at receiver+0x28, the receiver's own table and the two cdecl services.
return_semantics.ownership: the body performs no reference acquisition or release of its own. It reads a pointer out of the receiver, hands that pointer to three callees, and copies one dword out of the object at +0x28. Nothing it hands out is stored anywhere it owns.
return_semantics.lifetime: the 0x18-byte frame object is the body's own stack storage and dies with the call. 0x00427fd0, the +0x14 dispatch and 0x0093db80 are all handed the record inside it, so none of them retains it. The pointer the +0x24 dispatch published in the frame's leading word is read once and never stored by this body.

evidence.decompiler_disagreements: the live decompilation is used here as a hint and is contradicted by the listing in five places, each resolved in favour of the listing. (1) It opens with __fastcall and one int* parameter; the body ends in a bare RET with no immediate, so there is no argument slot, and the only incoming register read before the first write is ECX. (2) It writes the 0x00f9b84e/0x00f9b85d stores as uStack_a = 10 and uStack_c = 2, i.e. as two locals two bytes apart; the listing puts them four bytes apart in the machine, at entry-0x02 and entry-0x04. (3) It reads them in the wrong order relative to their addresses: it assigns uStack_a the 10 and uStack_c the 2, while the machine stores 10 at the HIGHER address. (4) It calls FUN_00427fd0 with param_1 + 0x205, i.e. the receiver's +0x814 word as a destination; the listing pushes that word's ADDRESS as the argument and puts the destination in ECX, and 0x00427fd0's own frame reads its argument at [EBP+8] and dereferences it while treating ECX as the destination. (5) It calls FUN_006b4b60(iVar4, uVar3), i.e. object-first; the listing pushes EAX (the lookup result) first and ESI (the object) second, so the argument order is reversed. It also drops the two stores' addresses and the frame offsets entirely, which is why none of its local names is used here.

unresolved_questions: The two indirect dispatches at 0x00f9b813 and 0x00f9b878 have no address, so their terminators cannot be read and their 8-byte cleanups are INFERRED. The inference is pinned three ways -- the frame requirement, the register-restoration consequence of the alternative, and the fact that only this value makes every stack-relative address land on a documented field -- but it cannot be confirmed from this binary. Resolving it needs a runtime capture of ESP across either call, or a caller of 0x00f9b7f0 whose own frame shows how much it expects back.

The identity of the three table entries (+0x24 and +0x14 on the object at receiver+0x28, +0x80 on the receiver) is unknown. They are reachable only through a table the objects name through their leading word, and this binary has no MSVC RTTI, so the table at 0x01490be8 identifies nothing on its own. The packages that already carry 0x0093db80 (pkg-dfw-006a2e20) do not cover them.

What the object at receiver+0x28 IS is not stated by any listing in this set. It is read at exactly one word, it is re-read three times, and it is handed to two table entries and one cdecl service. The receiver's word at +0x814 is likewise unnamed: the body only compares it against a candidate and takes its address. Naming either would be a member story the evidence does not carry.

The dword the +0x24 dispatch publishes in the frame's leading word (frame+0x00) is read exactly once, at 0x00f9b819, and is then treated as a pointer to a 0x14+-byte record. Nothing in this set writes that word after the dispatch and nothing shows what type the pointed-at record is beyond its +0x12 being compared with 0x0a. Whether it is the same kind of record as the one at frame+0x04 is NOT established: 0x00427fd0, which documents the frame+0x04 record's layout, is never handed frame+0x00.

The return type is inferred as void. Both records leave it open (abi.return_semantics 'unclassified_in_EAX', ghidra_function.return_type 'undefined') and the listing's three edges leave three different dead words in EAX. Nothing writes EAX for a caller, so void is the only reading consistent with the machine, but a differential run would settle it.

0x006b4b60's own body reads stack slots one through five (0x006b4b7f MOV EBP,[ESP+0x24], 0x006b4b8f MOV EAX,[ESP+0x30], 0x006b4bab MOV EBX,[ESP+0x2c], 0x006b4bd8 MOV EDI,[ESP+0x34]), while this call site pushes only two. Slots three through five therefore hold the caller's own frame and are read as if they were arguments. The body is 138 instructions and installs its own SEH scope, and this call site is inside that scope, so nothing crashes -- but the mismatch is unexplained by anything in this package and it means 0x006b4b60's real prototype is not the two-argument one this call site implies.

0x006b1f90's own frame does not close under any reading either: it pushes three words, and 0x00e5c780 must remove two of them for the body to balance, yet the value 0x00e5c780 leaves in the slot 0x006b1fa5 reads is not accounted for by anything in its 16 instructions. Both 0x006b1f90 and 0x006b4b60 read as service or thunk code rather than ordinary compiled functions, and neither has a metadata record. This does not affect the reconstruction -- both are modelled as observers with the signatures their own terminators and this call site's pushes fix -- but it is why their internals are not claimed.

The subsystem label 'Terrain' and the cluster 'terrain-world' come from the triage record, not from this body. Nothing in the listing, the callees or the vtable supports or contradicts it. The one fact that is suggestive -- the type code 0x000a compared at 0x00f9b81d, 0x00428009 and 0x0041ea10 -- is suggestive of nothing in particular, and no claim is made.
